# zcash-now

> zcash-now keeps AI coding agents current on Zcash. Orchard has been closed to new funds since NU6.3 (Ironwood), NU7 is live on testnet with 25-second blocks, and several older servers and libraries no longer work. Every fact names its source and when it was last checked.

Rules for agents writing Zcash code: use shielded funds and unified addresses; give servers a viewing key, never a spending key; let the SDK compute ZIP 317 fees; treat a payment as seen, then mined, then confirmed; keep personal data out of memos; never paste a seed phrase or key into a chat.

# Current Zcash facts

Updated 2026-11-04. Each fact says how it was checked: read (a source page), probe (a live server call) or run (a command that produced the result).

## Upgrades

- NU7 is active on testnet from height 4,465,026: blocks target 25 seconds, and v4 transactions are invalid. Replaces: "testnet blocks every 75 seconds", "v4 transactions". (testnet; [source](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/blob/eb38d7a373661179dbc083a2fd58b3a6c9b25818/components/zcash_protocol/src/consensus.rs), probe 2026-11-04)
- librustzcash set NU7's mainnet activation height to 3,543,405 on 21 Oct 2026. Mainnet was at height 3,541,302 on 4 Nov 2026, so at 75-second blocks activation is about 44 hours later. Zebra's mainnet readiness tracker (issue 11674) was still open. Replaces: "NU7 mainnet activation is not scheduled yet". (mainnet; [source](https://github.com/zcash/librustzcash/commit/f53a9b46e8), read 2026-11-04)
- NU6.3 (Ironwood) activated on mainnet at block 3,428,143 on 28 Jul 2026, and on testnet at height 4,134,000, after a flaw in Orchard's circuit that could have allowed counterfeit ZEC. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://www.theblock.co/news/ecosystems/2026-07-28-zcash-ironwood-upgrade-launching-new-shielded-pool-after-orchard-vulnerability-409934), read 2026-11-04)

## Pools

- Orchard accepts withdrawals only. New shielded funds go to the Ironwood pool. Replaces: "use the Orchard pool", "pool: 'orchard'", "orchard_zatoshi". (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), read 2026-11-04)

## Addresses

- Ironwood notes go to the Orchard receiver a unified address already carries, so existing u1 and utest1 addresses keep working. Replaces: "unified addresses need a new Ironwood receiver". (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://zechub.wiki/guides/zcash-devtool), read 2026-11-04)
- Testnet addresses start utest1 (unified), ztestsapling1 (Sapling) or tm (transparent). Coins on testnet are TAZ and have no value. (testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), read 2026-11-04)
- zcash-devtool's wallet init gives the account a default address with a transparent receiver. wallet generate-address with no --pool flag makes an address with shielded receivers only, which is the one to hand to payers. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://github.com/zcash/zcash-devtool), run 2026-11-04)

## Endpoints

- **works**: Use testnet.zec.rocks:443 (gRPC over TLS) as the testnet light-wallet server. (testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), probe 2026-11-04)
- **works**: zec.rocks:443 serves mainnet light-wallet clients over gRPC with TLS. (mainnet; [source](https://zcash-sdk.nym.com/guidance/), probe 2026-11-04)
- **broken**: The old testnet light-wallet servers lightwalletd.testnet.electriccoin.co and testnet.lightwalletd.com are dead. Replaces: "lightwalletd.testnet.electriccoin.co", "testnet.lightwalletd.com". (testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), probe 2026-11-04)

## Faucets

- **works**: Fauzec sends 1 TAZ per address every 24 hours to unified or Sapling addresses, shielded. Its web form has a Cloudflare Turnstile human check. A claim to a shielded-only unified address arrived in the Ironwood pool in transaction cc2d88b8… (version 6, NU7, height 4,581,808) and was spendable after about 10 confirmations. (testnet; [source](https://fauzec.com/), run 2026-11-04)
- **works**: Noir Wallet's testnet extension gives its own account a daily TAZ allowance; 1 TAZ arrived on 4 Nov 2026. The wallet can't send it on NU7 yet, so it is only useful for receiving. (testnet; [source](https://github.com/NoirWallet/noir-wallet/releases), run 2026-11-04)
- **broken**: Valar's faucet (0.125 TAZ per IP address every 24 hours) refused both a unified address and a Sapling address with "the wallet cannot pay this address", and had made no payouts in the previous 24 hours. Failed claims do not use up the daily allowance. (testnet; [source](https://faucet.testnet.valargroup.dev/), run 2026-11-04)
- **broken**: The Jino Labs faucet is paused for NU7. (testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), read 2026-11-04)
- At the Free Society Hack, post a utest1 address in the mentors chat and a Zcash mentor sends TAZ. (testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Privacy-track-Zcash-4073e52aeb1580e9b24fe57aeddb8b3e), read 2026-11-04)

## Explorers

- **works**: zexplorer.app shows a testnet transaction at /testnet/tx/<txid>, including version-6 NU7 transactions; the hack's agent guide recommends it. testnet.zcashexplorer.app shows them at /transactions/<txid> in a browser, blocks some scripted requests, and misreads Ironwood value: a 1 TAZ transfer into Ironwood showed "Transaction fee 1.00015 TAZ", because it counts the Orchard part of the transaction but not the Ironwood part. Take amounts and fees from the wallet. (testnet; [source](https://stadium.joinwebzero.com/programs/free-society-hack-2026/privacy/llms.txt), probe 2026-11-04)
- **broken**: zec.rocks runs explorer.testnet.zec.rocks (testnet) and explorer.zec.rocks (mainnet), but on 4 Nov 2026 both accepted connections and then returned HTTP 503 after about 38 seconds. Link to testnet.zcashexplorer.app instead. Replaces: "explorer.testnet.zec.rocks works". (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://forum.zcashcommunity.com/t/block-explorer-testnet-infrastructure-2025/51451/8), probe 2026-11-04)

## Sdks

- **works**: zcash-devtool, built from source (commit 0b3436b), creates a testnet wallet, syncs NU7 testnet, reports Ironwood balances and sends shielded Ironwood payments with memos (transaction c00460bf…, mined at height 4,581,860). It is for prototyping, not production. That commit pins librustzcash from 16 Oct 2026, before NU7's mainnet height was set, so rebuild against a newer pin before using it on mainnet. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://github.com/zcash/zcash-devtool), run 2026-11-04)
- **broken**: Noir Wallet's testnet extension receives TAZ and shows Ironwood balances, but on 4 Nov 2026 its sends on NU7 testnet failed with "transaction uses an incorrect consensus branch id": it signs for the upgrade before NU7, and its source has no testnet NU7 height or branch ID. Until that is fixed, pay from zcash-devtool. The SDK offers connect, getBalance, sendTransaction({ to, amount, memo, fundingSource }) and getTransactionHistory. Replaces: "Noir Wallet's testnet build can send on NU7 testnet". (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://github.com/NoirWallet/noir-wallet/releases), run 2026-11-04)
- **unverified**: Thus Spoke Zakura v0.4 runs a disposable local regtest network in Docker with NU7 and Ironwood active, a faucet and on-demand mining. Its API takes pool 'ironwood' and rejects 'orchard'. Replaces: "pool: 'orchard' in the Thus Spoke Zakura API". (testnet; [source](https://github.com/zcashlabs/thus-spoke-zakura/releases), read 2026-11-04)
- **unverified**: Zingolib has active Ironwood support work, and zshield-mcp reports real testnet payments through zingo-cli. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://github.com/Steeve-Crypto/zshield-mcp), read 2026-11-04)
- **unverified**: zkool2's zkool_graphql is a GraphQL wallet server with NU7 and Ironwood support, watch-only accounts from a viewing key, and built-in NEAR Intents and FROST. The hack's agent guide recommends it for backends and payment watchers. Run it with --allow-unauthenticated only on localhost: it then exposes seeds to anyone who can reach the port. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://stadium.joinwebzero.com/programs/free-society-hack-2026/privacy/llms.txt), read 2026-11-04)
- **broken**: WebZjs (@chainsafe/webzjs-wallet) is not on npm and has no Ironwood support. Building it needs Rust nightly, wasm-pack, just, yarn and a gRPC-web proxy. Replaces: "npm install @chainsafe/webzjs-wallet". (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), read 2026-11-04)
- **broken**: @zcash/monitor in ronykris/zcash-sdk wraps WebZjs, so it inherits WebZjs's NU7 problems. Its @zcash/uri package only builds ZIP 321 links. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://github.com/ronykris/zcash-sdk), read 2026-11-04)
- **broken**: zecli from crates.io makes Orchard-only addresses, which cannot receive funds. The git version needs a zidecar server, and none is hosted for testnet. Replaces: "cargo install zecli". (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), read 2026-11-04)
- **broken**: Zallet and zecd have no NU7 release. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), read 2026-11-04)
- **broken**: ZPay, the x402 facilitator with a spend-limited agent wallet, needs a self-hosted Zinder stack in Docker. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), read 2026-11-04)
- **unverified**: CipherPay is a hosted checkout that watches a merchant's viewing key and calls the merchant's server when a payment arrives. Its testnet is at testnet.cipherpay.app. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), read 2026-11-04)
- Frontier Compute's zcash-mcp is a read-only ZAP1 attestation server, not a wallet. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://github.com/Frontier-Compute/zcash-mcp), read 2026-11-04)

## Fees

- Under ZIP 317 the conventional fee is the marginal fee times the larger of 2 and the number of logical actions. The marginal fee is 5,000 zatoshis before Revision 2 and 1,000 from Revision 2. Let the wallet or SDK compute it. Replaces: "fee: 10000", "a fixed fee of 0.0001 ZEC". (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0317), read 2026-11-04)

## Payments

- Treat a payment as seen, then mined, then confirmed, and wait for more confirmations on larger amounts. At 25-second testnet blocks, 10 confirmations take about 4 minutes. Replaces: "a broadcast payment is a finished payment". (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), read 2026-11-04)
- Give a payment server a viewing key: it can see incoming payments but cannot spend them. Keep the spending key off the server. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://fancy-spectacles-44b.notion.site/Zcash-Developer-Resources-3ff3e52aeb1580a583c8e82b95a6f94e), read 2026-11-04)
- Fund payments from shielded balances. Transparent funding can reveal and link the coins it spends. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://github.com/NoirWallet/noir-wallet-sdk), read 2026-11-04)
- Memos go only to shielded recipients and hold at most 512 bytes. Put an order token in them, not personal data. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://github.com/NoirWallet/noir-wallet-sdk), read 2026-11-04)
- Keep ZEC amounts as decimal strings or integer zatoshis (1 ZEC is 100,000,000 zatoshis), never as floating-point numbers. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://github.com/NoirWallet/noir-wallet-sdk), read 2026-11-04)
- Payment links follow ZIP 321: zcash:<address>?amount=<ZEC with up to 8 decimals>&memo=<base64url, no padding>. Memos are only allowed for shielded addresses, and an unknown req- parameter makes the whole link invalid. (mainnet, testnet; [source](https://zips.z.cash/zip-0321), read 2026-11-04)

# Get testnet coins (TAZ) into a wallet

Recipe `get-test-coins-cli` for the cli stack, verified on 2026-11-04. Evidence: Fauzec sent 1 TAZ to a zcash-devtool shielded-only unified address in transaction cc2d88b88890805b8a216b20adbbb492c3541271764526c234dfb40e607a8df4 (version 6, NU7), mined at testnet height 4,581,808 into the Ironwood pool. It was spendable after about 10 confirmations.

## Steps

```bash
# A receive address with shielded receivers only, so a faucet can't pay a transparent receiver.
zdt wallet -w ./w generate-address

# Claim at https://fauzec.com/ with that address and complete the human check (1 TAZ per address every 24 hours).
# Or use Fauzec's API, which has no human check (documented in the hack's agent guide; not tried here yet):
#   curl -X POST https://fauzec.com/api/v1/claim -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"network":"testnet","address":"utest1..."}'
#   curl https://fauzec.com/api/v1/status/testnet/<request_id>   (repeat until the state is final; it then carries the txid)
# At the Free Society Hack, you can also post the address in the mentors chat.

# Check that it arrived, then wait until it is spendable.
zdt wallet -w ./w sync
zdt wallet -w ./w list-tx
zdt wallet -w ./w balance
```

## Expected output

- `list-tx` shows the transaction as `Mined:` with `Output 0 (Ironwood)` and the value, received by your address. There is no sender address: shielded payments don't reveal one.
- `balance` shows the amount in `Balance:` straight away, and in `Ironwood Spendable:` after about 10 confirmations (about 4 minutes at 25-second blocks).
- `zcash_tx_status` on the transaction ID reports version 6 and consensus branch `77190ad9` (NU7).

## Gotchas

- Valar's faucet refused unified and Sapling addresses on 4 Nov 2026 ("the wallet cannot pay this address"), and the Jino Labs faucet is paused for NU7.
- Noir Wallet's testnet extension gives its own account a daily allowance, but it can't send on NU7 yet, so those coins can't be moved to another wallet.
- Testnet explorers can't show amounts or addresses, and testnet.zcashexplorer.app misreports the fee on Orchard-to-Ironwood transfers. Read amounts from the wallet.

## Privacy

- The faucet sees your IP address next to the address you claim with. Use a fresh address from `generate-address` for faucets, not one you publish elsewhere.
- TAZ has no value, but the address and its keys work the same way on mainnet. Keep the wallet folder and identity file private.

# Connect Noir Wallet and send a shielded payment from a web app

Recipe `noir-connect-send-react` for the react stack, unverified on 2026-11-04. Evidence: Written from the @noir-wallet/sdk README and the wallet's source. On 4 Nov 2026 the testnet extension received TAZ, but a send from it failed on NU7 testnet with "transaction uses an incorrect consensus branch id", so sendTransaction will fail on testnet until Noir supports NU7.

## Known problem (4 Nov 2026)

Noir Wallet's testnet build signs transactions for the network upgrade before NU7, and testnet nodes reject them: "transaction uses an incorrect consensus branch id". Receiving and balances work. Until Noir ships NU7 support, pay from zcash-devtool (the send-shielded recipe), and use Noir only to receive.

## Install the testnet wallet

1. Open the [Noir Wallet releases](https://github.com/NoirWallet/noir-wallet/releases) and download the asset ending in `-testnet.zip` (v1.0.40 or later).
2. Unzip it, open `chrome://extensions`, turn on Developer mode and choose Load unpacked.
3. Check that the extension is named `[Testnet] Noir Wallet`. Mainnet and testnet are separate extensions; `switchNetwork()` always throws.

## Code

```bash
npm install @noir-wallet/sdk
```

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import { getNoirWallet } from '@noir-wallet/sdk';

export function PayButton({ to, amount, memo }: { to: string; amount: string; memo: string }) {
  const [status, setStatus] = useState('');

  async function pay() {
    // getNoirWallet() is null during server rendering or without the extension.
    const wallet = getNoirWallet();
    if (!wallet) return setStatus('Install the Noir Wallet testnet extension first.');
    const { zcash } = wallet;
    try {
      // connect() opens an approval window, so call it from a click.
      if (!(await zcash.getAccounts())) await zcash.connect();
      const txid = await zcash.sendTransaction({ to, amount, memo, fundingSource: 'shielded' });
      setStatus(`Sent ${txid}. Waiting for it to be mined.`);
    } catch (error) {
      setStatus(error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Wallet request failed');
    }
  }

  return (
    <div>
      <button onClick={pay}>Pay {amount} TAZ</button>
      <p>{status}</p>
    </div>
  );
}
```

## Gotchas

- Amounts are decimal ZEC strings, for example `'0.01'`. The field is `to`, not `address`.
- A memo needs a shielded recipient and holds at most 512 UTF-8 bytes.
- The wallet's approval screen sets the final fee. `getMaxTransfer()` estimates the most you can send.
- `sendTransaction` returns once the transaction is broadcast. Check `zcash_tx_status` or `getTransactionHistory()` for mined and confirmed.

## Privacy

- `fundingSource: 'shielded'` keeps the payment fully shielded. Transparent funding can reveal and link the coins it spends.
- Your site learns the connected account's addresses and balance. Ask only for what the flow needs.
- For identity, `signMessage(message, { signingMode: 'derived' })` gives a key that is unlinkable to the main transparent address.

# Build a ZIP 321 payment link

Recipe `payment-link-node` for the node stack, partial on 2026-11-04. Evidence: The builder below is the one in zcash-now's src/zip321.ts, and its unit tests check the ZIP 321 rules for amounts, memos, req- parameters and duplicates. No wallet has paid one of its links yet.

## The format

`zcash:<address>?amount=<ZEC>&memo=<base64url>&message=<percent-encoded text>`

- Amounts are decimal ZEC with 1 to 8 decimal places, for example `0.01`. No other separators.
- Memos are base64url (`-` and `_`) with no `=` padding, at most 512 bytes, and only for shielded addresses. A memo on a transparent address makes the whole link invalid.
- An unknown parameter starting with `req-` makes the link invalid. Other unknown parameters are ignored.

## Code

```js
const SHIELDED = /^(?:u1|utest1|zs1|ztestsapling1)[02-9ac-hj-np-z]+$/;

export function paymentLink({ address, amount, memo, message }) {
  const params = [];
  if (amount !== undefined) {
    if (!/^\d+(?:\.\d{1,8})?$/.test(amount)) throw new Error('amount: decimal ZEC, up to 8 decimals');
    params.push(`amount=${amount}`);
  }
  if (memo !== undefined) {
    if (!SHIELDED.test(address)) throw new Error('memos need a shielded address');
    const bytes = Buffer.from(memo, 'utf8');
    if (bytes.length > 512) throw new Error('memo: at most 512 bytes');
    params.push(`memo=${bytes.toString('base64url')}`);
  }
  if (message !== undefined) params.push(`message=${encodeURIComponent(message)}`);
  return `zcash:${address}${params.length ? `?${params.join('&')}` : ''}`;
}

// paymentLink({ address: 'utest1...', amount: '0.01', memo: 'order 7f3a' })
// -> zcash:utest1...?amount=0.01&memo=b3JkZXIgN2YzYQ
```

Show the link as a QR code (for example with the `qrcode` npm package) and as a button. Noir Wallet can pay the same request with `sendTransaction`; see the noir-connect-send recipe.

## Gotchas

- Keep amounts as strings. `0.29 * 1e8` in JavaScript is `28999999.999999996`.
- Give payers an address with shielded receivers only (zcash-devtool `generate-address`), so a wallet can't fall back to a transparent receiver.

## Privacy

- The link itself is not on-chain, but anyone who sees it learns the address, amount and memo. Send it over a private channel.
- Use a random order token as the memo, not the buyer's name or email.

# Send a shielded payment from the command line

Recipe `send-shielded-cli` for the cli stack, verified on 2026-11-04. Evidence: zcash-devtool built from commit 0b3436b sent 0.1 TAZ from Ironwood to a Noir Wallet unified address with the memo "trial 1" in transaction c00460bfaef41be5147089572189c5548bf1fbc6454e1b532c09f9c717d06abe (version 6, NU7), mined at testnet height 4,581,860. The fee was 0.00025 TAZ.

## Before you start

- Rust 1.89 or later, and Git. The release build takes about 4 minutes.
- A few TAZ from Fauzec or a hack mentor. Valar's faucet refused shielded addresses on 4 Nov 2026.

## Steps

```bash
git clone https://github.com/zcash/zcash-devtool.git
cd zcash-devtool
cargo build --release
alias zdt="$PWD/target/release/zcash-devtool"

# New testnet wallet. The seed is encrypted to the age identity file, which is
# created if it does not exist. With no terminal on stdin, an empty line makes a new seed.
zdt wallet -w ./w init --name demo -i ./w-identity.txt -n test < /dev/null

# A receive address with shielded receivers only. Give this one to payers and faucets.
zdt wallet -w ./w generate-address

# After funding: sync, then check that the funds are spendable.
zdt wallet -w ./w sync
zdt wallet -w ./w balance

# Send 0.01 TAZ with a memo. --value is in zatoshis (1 TAZ = 100,000,000).
zdt wallet -w ./w send -i ./w-identity.txt --address <utest1...> --value 1000000 --memo "order 7f3a"
zdt wallet -w ./w list-tx
```

## Expected output

- `sync` logs `Scan complete for range ChainTip(...)`.
- `balance` prints `Height:` and spendable lines for Sapling, Orchard, Ironwood and Unshielded funds. New shielded funds land in Ironwood.
- `send` broadcasts the transaction. Check it with `zcash_tx_status`: seen, then mined, then confirmed.

## Gotchas

- The default server is zec.rocks, which is `testnet.zec.rocks:443` on testnet. `-s` picks another.
- The address `init` creates also has a transparent receiver. `generate-address` with no `--pool` flag leaves it out.
- `--pool orchard` on `generate-address` is still right for Ironwood: Ironwood notes use the Orchard receiver.
- Received funds need confirmations before they are spendable. Funds from another wallet took about 10 confirmations (4 minutes at 25-second blocks).
- `send` splits change into several notes (up to `--target-note-count`, default 4), so later sends don't wait for change to confirm.
- If `send` fails after `Sending transaction...` (for example `peer closed connection`), the signed transaction is already saved and its coins are locked. Don't send again: `list-tx` shows it as Unmined with an expiry height. Rebroadcast the saved bytes (`transactions.raw` in the wallet's `data.sqlite`) with lightwalletd's `SendTransaction` before that height, or wait for expiry to release the coins.

## Privacy

- Amounts, sender and receiver are shielded on-chain. The memo is readable by the recipient and anyone holding their viewing key, so put an order token in it, not personal data.
- The light-wallet server sees your IP address and when you sync. On a watched network, add `--connection tor` to `sync` and `send`.
- Keep `w-identity.txt` and the `w` folder out of git and out of every chat.

# Watch for incoming payments with a viewing key

Recipe `watch-payments-cli` for the cli stack, partial on 2026-11-04. Evidence: A view-only wallet was created with init-fvk from a testnet account's unified full viewing key, without printing the key, then synced; list-tx --mode csv printed its header. Detecting an actual payment has not run yet because no payment has been sent to it.

## Why a viewing key

A server holding the unified full viewing key (UFVK) can see payments to the account but cannot spend them. Keep the spending key, and the wallet that holds it, off the server.

## Steps

```bash
# On the machine that holds the spending key: the account's keys.
# list-accounts prints the UFVK. Copy it into the server's secret store, never into a chat.
zdt wallet -w ./w list-accounts

# On the server: a view-only wallet from that UFVK. --birthday is a block height
# before the first payment you expect; it defaults to the current height.
zdt wallet -w ./watch init-fvk --name shop --fvk "$ZCASH_UFVK"
zdt wallet -w ./watch sync

# One CSV row per output. The last column is the memo, which carries your order token.
zdt wallet -w ./watch list-tx --mode csv
```

## Matching orders by memo (Node)

```js
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';

const zdt = (...args) => execFileSync('zcash-devtool', ['wallet', '-w', './watch', ...args], { encoding: 'utf8' });

export function paidOrderTokens() {
  zdt('sync');
  const [, ...rows] = zdt('list-tx', '--mode', 'csv').trim().split('\n');
  // The memo is the last column; order tokens contain no commas.
  return new Set(rows.map((row) => row.slice(row.lastIndexOf(',') + 1).trim()).filter(Boolean));
}
```

Run it after each block (about every 25 seconds on testnet). Mark an order paid when its token appears, and fulfil it after enough confirmations: `list-tx --json` gives each transaction's `mined_height`, and `zcash_tx_status` gives confirmations.

## Gotchas

- `sync` only sees mined transactions, so the first sighting is already "mined", not "seen".
- Use a fresh random token per order (for example 8 hex characters) so a memo can't be guessed or reused.
- `list-tx --json` emits only `txid` and `mined_height`. Use `--mode csv` for memos.

## Privacy

- The UFVK reveals every incoming and outgoing payment of that account to whoever holds it, so store it like a password.
- The light-wallet server sees the server's IP address and sync pattern. Run the watcher with `--connection tor` if that matters.
- Store order tokens, not names or emails, next to payments.
